guidelines.detail: same as LRN-040 (The description and missing-flow records support preserving the stated transitions and concurrent work in the BPMN structure. This wording is not tied to the process and is essentially covered by learned guideline LRN-040.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The generic start label loses the meaningful trigger in the description; the message-to-friends label pair also illustrates the importance of preserving the described action. This guideline is already covered by FID-03, which requires short, faithful labels.)

refines COL-01 (The description explicitly states that an architect returns a draft and that online stores process orders, while the records show the corresponding pools and message flows are absent. This refines COL-01 by specifying a clear observable cue for modeling an external participant as a pool. Ordinary external mentions without stated interaction are not sufficient.)

refines FID-01 (The description places ordering after preparing the materials list, but the generated model lacks the ordering activity and the flow to it. This makes the general instruction to model every described activity more specific for this situation.)

same as LRN-061 (The label pairs show both generic labels and labels whose meaning diverges from or alters the described action or decision. The proposed guideline is essentially the same as learned guideline LRN-061; it also aligns with documented guideline FID-03's direction to use short, faithful labels.)

same as LRN-063 (The description states that external participants receive information or orders and respond or process them, while the reference has pools and message flows with no generated counterparts. LRN-063 already gives essentially the same modeling instruction.)

documentation rule FLOW-01 not applied (The cited records show missing sequence flows where the reference preserves ordering or dependencies stated in the description. FLOW-01 already directs using sequence flows to represent execution order between flow nodes in the same scope, so this guideline is already documented.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The label pairs show generated labels that are generic or shift the stated meaning, including the process trigger and refinement decision. FID-03 already advises short, faithful labels and meaningful event triggers, so this guideline is already documented.)

documentation rule COL-01 not applied (The description explicitly states requests to external participants and responses or order processing, while the records show the corresponding participants and message flows absent from the generated model. COL-01 already requires representing every distinct participant as a pool, so this guideline is already covered by documented guidance; LRN-063 also expresses essentially the same situation.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one activity, event, or event outcome leads to another, including after a wait or along an alternative event path: Model sequence flows connecting the corresponding BPMN nodes in the described order, preserving transitions into and out of waiting events and each described alternative path.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an ordering between activities or events, or says that one activity proceeds while another is underway

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity, event, or decision with a meaningful action, object, or condition

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies an external participant as receiving a request or information and explicitly states that the participant responds or processes it: model the external participant as a separate pool and represent the stated exchanges with message flows between appropriate communication and receipt elements
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies an external participant as receiving a request or information and explicitly states that the participant responds or processes it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When When the description states that prepared items are ordered.: Model ordering as a distinct activity after the preparation activity, with a sequence flow connecting them.
rules_sent_back.situation: When the description states that prepared items are ordered.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity or decision with a particular action, condition, scope, or criterion: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or gateway concisely and faithfully, preserving distinctions relevant to the described action or decision rather than substituting unrelated meaning.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity or decision with a particular action, condition, scope, or criterion

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly orders activities or states that one activity follows or depends on another

rules_sent_back.instruction: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies an external participant who receives a request or information and explicitly states that the participant responds or processes it
